In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of the interaction between HPV16 E6 and p53.
the role of DNA methylation in HPV16 early genes expression.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miR-375 is upregulated by DNA demethylation and this leads to the repression of HPV16 E6 mRNA expression.
miR-375 upregulation is a consequence of 5azadC-induced demethylation of the HPV16 L1 gene and that this upregulation is responsible for the downregulation of the viral E6 gene.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-azacytidine treatment represses HPV 16 E6 expression by upregulating miR-375 levels in cervical cancer cell lines.
HPV E6 and E2 are both regulated by epigenetic events and that E2 regulation is more important than E6 regulation in cervical carcinogenesis.
the 5azadC induced miR-375 upregulation leads to HPV16 E6 repression in an E2 independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epigenetic modifications, in the form of methylation, may be involved in HPV16 oncogenic potential.
DNA methylation is a key regulator of HPV early gene expression.
the epigenetic status of the viral DNA plays a role in regulating viral gene expression and thus may be an important contributor to the progression of HPV-associated cancers.
